Short answer: Yes — as of today (September 4, 2026) Irish VAT on digitally supplied/electronic services is charged at the Irish standard VAT rate, which is 23%. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-on-services/electronic-services/vat-and-electronically-supplied-services/index.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Key points and a couple of caveats:
- Revenue (the Irish tax authority) treats telecommunications, broadcasting and electronically supplied services as taxable at the standard rate. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-on-services/electronic-services/vat-and-electronically-supplied-services/index.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- Ireland’s standard VAT rate is 23% (the published Revenue pages and recent budget material show the standard rate at 23%). ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/E/electronic-services.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- Exceptions/operational notes you should be aware of before sending the PDF: if the purchaser is a VAT‑registered business outside Ireland the reverse‑charge/B2B rules or OSS registration may apply; and small cross‑border thresholds/domestic registration rules (e.g., the €10,000 threshold for TBE supplies affecting domestic VAT treatment) can change how you account for VAT. Check the Revenue guidance for those rules. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-on-services/electronic-services/vat-and-electronically-supplied-services/index.aspx?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can:
- Draft a one‑line correction for your PDF (e.g., “As at September 4, 2026 the Irish VAT rate applying to digital/electronic services is 23% — Revenue guidance”).  
- Or update the paragraph with the brief caveats above (B2B reverse charge, OSS, threshold note) and include links/citations. Which would you prefer?
